New words — 29

Repair — six that got away on first listen

diǎnzàn

to like (a post)

diǎn + zàn — 'tap the praise'. It's the like-button verb: posts, photos, Moments. You heard it in the quiz but the meaning didn't surface.
Gěi wǒ de péngyǒuquān diǎnzàn ba!
juéjuézi

amazing (cutesy)

Internet-slang 'amazing' — mostly written, playful tone. Three even syllables: jué-jué-zi. If a friend texts it, they're delighted.
Zhège dàngāo wèidào juéjuézi!
hǎodī / hǎodā

okie!

Two spellings of the cute 'okie' — hǎodī (texting-cute) and hǎodā (cutest). One card, two readings, both mean 'okay!' — that's why the quiz tag has a slash.
Hǎodā, wǒ máshàng lái!
dào shíhou zài shuō

we'll see / decide later

A frozen four-word stamp — 'decide when the time comes'. Never rebuild it word-by-word; take it whole. And remember day 8's insight: after a concrete plan it's often a soft no.
Gǎitiān ma, dào shíhou zài shuō.
nānggè 🌶️

how / why

standard reading: zěnme

Chongqing 'how / why' — zěnme's local twin. Lock the sound, not the spelling: nāng (dipping) + gè. Missed it by ear on day 7 — re-hear it until it pops.
Nǐ nānggè bú gāoxìng le?
xiǎodé 🌶️

to know

standard reading: zhīdào

Chongqing 'to know' — zhīdào's local twin. Two quick falling syllables. You recognized it when reading but not when listening — that's the gap to close.
Nǐ xiǎodé ma?

hey!

usually pronounced hēi; the "hāi" spelling you may see is a variant. (verify)

topic-switch token — the everyday way to drop a new subject into a chat.

Maybe, so, all, plus — connectives

maybe, perhaps

Yěxǔ míngtiān xià yǔ

so, therefore

Wǒ hěn lèi, suǒyǐ bú qù le

all (of)

suǒyǒu needs its dōu — "suǒyǒu rén lái le" sounds unfinished.
Suǒyǒu rén dōu lái le

also; plus; one more

Hái yǒu yí ge wèntí

and; yet (written)

bookish connector — recognize it, but say érqiě ("moreover") or dànshì ("but") instead.
Ér tā, shénme dōu méi shuō

how about / or else

the proposal engine: yàobu… ba? "how about we…?"; also "otherwise" (kuài yìdiǎn, yàobu chídào le).
Yàobu wǒmen jiào wàimài ba?

plural suffix

toneless; only attaches to pronouns and people words (tāmen, háizimen).
Háizimen zài wán

Zhèxiē dōu shì wǒ de

zhòng (4th tone) = to hit/win (zhòngjiǎng "won a prize"); zhǒng (3rd tone) = kind/type — three tones, three words.

Verbs with attitude — help, act-as, only-then, hit/make

to help

bàng (4th tone) = "awesome" (day 12) — different word.
Wǒ lái bāng nǐ ba

to act as; when

Tā xiànzài dāng lǎoshī

only then; not until

jiù is the mirror image — "as early as/already" (bā diǎn jiù shuì le = in bed by eight).
Tā shí'èr diǎn cái chī fàn

to hit; make (a call); play

the great light-verb — dǎ diànhuà (call), dǎ chē (taxi), dǎ qiú (play ball), dǎ yóuxì (game).
Wǒ gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà

kànjian is the chatty twin of kàndào; jiàndào = meeting a person.

words, speech

huà also = "to draw" and the noun "drawing" (huà yì zhāng huà — "draw a picture") — the Sunday sweep has that twin.
Shuōhuà a!

question suffix

toneless, never standalone — it lives inside shénme, zěnme, duōme.

Glue — grammar

bǐ "A is Adj-er than B"

Template: A + bǐ + B + Adj

ranking opinions — food, prices, cities, people

Chóngqìng de xiàtiān bǐ Běijīng rè duō le.
Zhège bǐ nàge hǎokàn.

Foreigner traps

  • No hěn inside the frame: bǐ + hěn + Adj is the classic learner slip — degree words gèng or hái sit before the adjective instead (bǐ wǒ gèng kuài).
  • The compared item follows bǐ: Wǒ bǐ nǐ gāo = I'm taller than you — flip the two nouns and you flip the verdict.
  • duō le / yìdiǎn after the adjective grade the gap (rè duō le = way hotter) — plain bǐ…rè leaves the margin unsaid, and natives usually say it.

méiyǒu "A is not as Adj as B"

Template: A + méiyǒu + B + Adj

the soft negative comparison

Jīntiān méiyǒu zuótiān máng.
Zhè jiā méiyǒu nà jiā gānjìng.

Foreigner traps

  • méiyǒu (not-as) vs bù bǐ (not MORE than — admits equal or better): méiyǒu nǐ kuài = slower than you; bù bǐ nǐ màn = certainly no slower than you.
  • The adjective stays on the positive property: méiyǒu + rè/hǎochī/gānjìng — there is no méiyǒu lěng for 'colder than'; say bǐ…lěng.
  • This méiyǒu is comparison, not 'didn't have' — it runs fast and light into the next word; the 'didn't have' one lands on the yǒu.

Native notes — comparing safely, the hum of agreement, and cái's complaint

bǐ compares things, not faces

Ranking dishes, cities, prices is small-talk gold. Turning the comparison on the person you're talking to (nǐ bǐ tā shuài) is touchy unless you're close friends teasing — and even then the tease lands harder than in English. Compare the dumplings, not the dinner guests.

ǹg… ǹg… ō! is the hum of listening

On calls and voice notes you'll hear a steady stream of soft ǹg and ō — that's not impatience, it's backchannel: 'I'm here, I follow.' Going silent while someone talks reads as cold or distracted. In texting the equivalent is short reactions — duì duì, shì ba — which is why a long heartfelt message answered with nothing feels like a slap.

cái complains, jiù brags

The mirror pair carries attitude, not just time: bā diǎn jiù dào le (there by eight — early, willing) vs shí'èr diǎn cái lái (didn't show till noon — the cái drips complaint about the lateness). Say the time, then choose your particle like a tone of voice: it's the difference between reporting and gossiping.

dǎ is the universal activity verb

dǎ diànhuà, dǎ chē, dǎ qiú, dǎ yóuxì, dǎ zhāohu — when an activity takes an object and some doing, try dǎ before hunting for a fancy verb. It's the single most useful catch-all in casual speech, and using it instead of bookish verbs is a register upgrade.
